item.title: Tyson Fury Was Desperate to Make Mega Money but Now Brands His ‘Hundreds of Millions’ Fortune as ‘Pointless’
item.description: ZUMAPRESS.com / MEGA Former heavyweight boxing champion Tyson Fury has admitted chasing a huge bank balance was his sole motivation during the second half of his boxing career – but he now views his vast wealth as “useless”. Speaking on The Louis Theroux Podcast on November 25, the 38-year-old British boxer reflected on how winning every world title during his first 27 unbeaten bouts left him financially unfulfilled after taxes, prompting him to instruct London sports lawyer Robert Davis to chase the biggest paydays in the United States rather than championships or legacy. “I’ve had all the belts. It didn’t make me happy, so I want all the money and I’m gonna see if that makes me happy,” Fury recalled telling Davis. “I said, ‘I’m not interested in belts. I’m not interested in legacies. I’m not interested in nothing.’ I said, ‘I want to make as much money as possible for me and my family.’ I said, ‘I’ve had all the belts and had no money.’ I said, ‘Now I want all the money and no belts.’ “That was always the plan, to make as much money as possible on the second journey.” According to The Sunday Times Rich List 2026 , Fury’s net worth is an estimated £162 million, around $211.6 million . ZUMAPRESS.com / MEGA While the boxer amassed a massive fortune from blockbuster U.S. fights, Fury told podcast host Louis Theroux , 56, that wealth has failed to bring him satisfaction. “This might sound very strange, but through all the fame and all the success and all the boxing fights and all the money and all the nothing … I think it’s all pointless, all of it,” Fury said, quoting the biblical Book of Ecclesiastes. “It leads me straight back to what Solomon said, ‘Everything is pointless.’ “All your achievements, all your goals, all your money, all your fame, it’s all a load of rubbish, and time’s fleeting. That’s the most important thing. “I sit here today with hundreds of millions in me bank, achieved everything there is to achieve in boxing, won every belt, can go, do, buy anything I want. “I don’t want anything. I don’t want to go anywhere.” Fury now lives a quieter life on the Isle of Man, but he regrets missing precious time with his wife Paris Fury , 36, and their children – Venezuela , 17, Prince John James , 15, Prince Tyson II , 10, Valencia , 8, Prince Adonis , 7, Athena 5, and Prince Rico , 3 – while chasing millions. He added: “What was it all for? If you’ve got 50 pence on you or you’ve got 10 million, you can only do the same things as anybody else anyway. “And everybody gets to the same destination point, that’s straight to the grave, sooner or later. And all the stuff in between is just hot air.” The Louis Theroux Podcast is available on Spotify and wherever you get your podcasts. item.title: Khang, a longtime fixture at 97.1 The Ticket, announces his departure
item.description: SOUTHFIELD — Truth be told, Khang Huynh really wanted an internship at WDFN. He didn't get it. Instead, he settled for one at WXYT. And his admitted second choice led to a run of two-plus decades, including nearly 20 years as producer of the Karsch & Anderson midday show. Huynh announced Tuesday, Nov. 24, that he is leaving the station. His last show working with Doug Karsch and Scott Anderson is Wednesday, Nov. 25. Huynh broke the news early during the 10 a.m. hour of Tuesday's show. "For the last 22 years ... I got to live out a dream, man. I got to talk sports for a living," Huynh, 46, said on air Tuesday. "This was my actual job. I never took that for granted. I know a lot of people would love to do what I got to do. "For everyone who actually has a real job and listened to the show, thank you." Later, in an interview with The News, Huynh said he wasn't prepared to make any specific announcements about his future plans. For now, he is calling himself a "media free agent." He said the decision to leave was his choice, and in the short-term, he plans to take some time off, and spend more time with his family, including his wife and two young children. He said a lengthy vacation is in the cards. Huynh joined WXYT back when the station was a staple on the AM dial, at 1270. He began as an intern for a host who was let go shortly after Huynh started. The station then launched the "Sports Inferno" show, hosted by a young host from Lansing, Mike Valenti, and veteran Detroit News columnist Terry Foster. Huynh began working for that show, and two months later, the show's assistant producer quit. Valenti asked Huynh if he was interested. Despite a lack of operations training, Huynh said yes, he underwent a two-week "crash course" in learning how to run the board, and he eventually got the job. Just like that, a lengthy career "behind the glass" was born for a guy who grew up with visions of being the next James Brown — the football commentator, not the singer. "Mike and Terry really liked me," Huynh said. "They really believed in me." Eventually, Valenti and Foster moved to afternoon drive, and Huynh remained at middays for a new show hosted by Karsch and Anderson, who will celebrate 20 years together in January. Huynh has been the only producer for Karsch and Anderson ("Gator") — a stable fixture in an industry known for its turnover. Huynh has been at the station since before WXYT began simulcasting on FM, at 97.1. That move to FM, in October 2007, proved a gamechanger in the local sports-talk radio war, as WXYT overtook WDFN for good. Now, 97.1 is the undisputed — and, for years, unchallenged — heavyweight champ of sports-talk radio ratings in Metro Detroit. It's a force all over Michigan and has a nationwide audience, too, since 97.1 began simulcasting its shows across the state in December 2025, and began airing shows on SiriusXM satellite radio earlier this year. item.title: College football is sacrificing its greatest rivalries at the altar of the 24-team playoff
item.description: Of all the many reasons to loathe the impending 24-team College Football Playoff — the schedule bloat, the likely terrible first- and second-round games, the defining downward of the concept of “playoff-worthy” teams, the all-encompassing greed — the worst might just be the devaluing of rivalry games. Once the heart and soul of the college football season, rivalry games are now just one more step in the ladder toward the playoff. And unless you’re sitting on 3 or 4 losses already — in which case, you really should’ve taken care of business in September and October — a rivalry game is now nothing more than a seeding mechanism. Consider how many great rivalry games college football rolls out on the final weekend of November: The Game. The Iron Bowl. The Egg Bowl. Consider how many times those games have had a direct, material impact on the way the season’s final rankings played out. And now consider the fact that, from a national perspective, they’re basically irrelevant except for bragging purposes. Bragging’s not nothing — there’s nothing quite like walking into work the Monday after a victory over your rival, finding one of their alumni, and offering up a casual “Catch the game on Saturday?” But bragging works best when you’ve obliterated your rival’s season by torpedoing their postseason hopes. If you can’t make the postseason, well, might as well drag someone down into hell along with you. With 24 teams in the postseason mix, though, even a rivalry loss will cost virtually every playoff contender just a few spots in the bracket. Of the 10 or so games this weekend with playoff implications, only one — USC-UCLA — is even close to a loser-goes-home match. And the ones where an upset could bounce the favorite from the playoffs — Indiana-Purdue, Oregon-Washington, maybe Texas Tech-TCU and Tennessee-Vanderbilt — won’t be potential elimination matchups next year. If the 24-team playoff were in place, you’d be looking at four-loss teams like Ole Miss and Florida trying to shamble their way into the playoff against Mississippi State and Florida State. Four losses! Johnny Vaught and Steve Spurrier would pack up and head to the lake before they’d entertain the idea of a team that lost a third of its games competing for a national championship. But more playoff teams means more revenue, no matter how damaged and undeserving those teams might be. Rivalry games, in the grand scheme of things, now rank behind five playoff round games in terms of weight and significance. In the past, a win over Alabama has meant storming the field for Auburn fans. But will it warrant the same celebration next year, with a 24-team playoff possibly making the game about nothing more than seeding? item.title: Report: Newcastle United Set for Ownership Changes as PIF Seeks Investment
item.description: Report: Newcastle United Set for Ownership Changes as PIF Seeks Investment Newcastle United Owners PIF Seeking Fresh Investment Through 25 Per Cent Stake Newcastle United’s ownership structure could be set for its most significant change since the Saudi Arabian Public Investment Fund (PIF) completed its takeover in 2021. Plans are underway to attract fresh investment through the issuing of new shares, potentially allowing outside investors to acquire up to 25 per cent of the club. As reported by David Ornstein and Chris Waugh of The Athletic , JP Morgan has been appointed to oversee the process, with discussions already taking place with interested parties. Crucially, the proposed arrangement would see money injected directly into Newcastle United. PIF would receive none of the proceeds, with its existing 84 per cent shareholding diluted as a consequence. The Reuben family currently owns the remaining 16 per cent. PIF Investment Strategy at Newcastle United Football ownership has increasingly become an exercise in asset development. Newcastle, purchased for £305 million in 2021, represent a particularly interesting example of that approach. There is reportedly a belief within the club that Newcastle could eventually command a valuation of approximately £5 billion. Achieving anything approaching that figure will require considerable investment in infrastructure, commercial operations and the playing squad. PIF’s withdrawal from several overseas investments, including its reported £3.7 billion commitment to LIV Golf, will inevitably encourage speculation about its intentions on Tyneside. Stadium Plans Driving Newcastle Investment The most pressing question surrounding Newcastle’s development concerns their stadium. Chief executive David Hopkinson has sought to accelerate progress on infrastructure projects that have become a source of considerable frustration among supporters. Photo IMAGO Newcastle announced plans in August for a £190 million “world-class” training complex at Woolsington Hall, with the intention of moving into the facility ahead of the 2029-30 season. Hopkinson has also indicated that supporters could receive clarity over the stadium situation “soon”. Expanding St James’ Park could cost approximately £500 million, while constructing a new stadium on neighbouring Leazes Park could exceed £1.3 billion. Either project would require substantial financial commitments, combining equity investment with external borrowing. Attracting new shareholders represents a logical mechanism for financing such an undertaking. Newcastle’s Long-Term Ambitions Hopkinson has previously outlined Newcastle’s ambition to be “in the debate about being the top club in the world” by 2030. item.title: Josh Downs shares what Travis Kelce is doing to help him during games for the Chiefs
item.description: Photo by Scott Winters/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Josh Downs has proven to be a solid addition to the Kansas City Chiefs, having racked up over 50 receiving yards in each of his opening two games. The wide receiver will need to fully earn the trust of quarterback Patrick Mahomes, but he is certainly on the right track. Adding another wideout was of real significance for the Chiefs before the trade deadline, and the veterans inside the building are certainly taking him under their wing. Travis Kelce and Mahomes have just as big an impact away from the field as they do on it, which is why Downs has massively appreciated how Kelce has been helping him to develop since joining the team earlier in the month. Josh Downs shares how Travis Kelce has been helping him at the Chiefs Downs caught his first touchdown for the Chiefs in his very first game, which came against the Atlanta Falcons. He has still only had around two weeks to work with the team, which has made Kelce’s help invaluable. “They’re helping me out out there. Obviously, I’ve only been here probably less than two weeks, so they’re still helping me out with a lot of stuff. Coming out of the play call, they’re telling me what to do. Even though I may know, they’re still telling me what to do. Kelce’s helping me at the line of scrimmage and stuff, so I appreciate them, and I’ve just got to try to keep building the trust. Kelce does too,” Downs told reporter Steve Walls. The 25-year-old was able to tally up another 59 receiving yards on Sunday against the Arizona Cardinals, which is solid considering he is still settling himself into the new team. The Chiefs will be hoping that Downs can get fully up to speed by the time they will be playing in the postseason. Playing alongside the likes of Kelce every day in practice will be a huge help for Downs, with the wideout clearly still having a fair amount to learn in Kansas City. “Even on that last play when I took that hit, he was just telling me, “Good play, just try to be a little more aware of that guy outside and maybe try to stay away from him a little bit more.” I think that was good advice from him, and I definitely can take that because I know he’s in situations like that all the time over the middle. He has a lot of awareness. I watch him, he also helps me, and he tells me stuff,” Downs added. According to the latest reports, the Los Angeles Clippers have been actively attempting to showcase their veterans in an attempt to trade them. item.title: Dai Dai Ames powers Tennessee past Maryland to open Players Era 16 Tournament
item.description: Nov 24, 2026; Las Vegas, Nevada, USA; Tennessee guard Dai Dai Ames (4) drives to the basket as Maryland forward Tomislav Buljan (23) looks to defend during the second half of an opening round game of the Players Era Sixteen tournament at Michelob Ultra Arena. Mandatory Credit: Candice Ward-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Tennessee and Maryland tipped off the Players Era 16 Tournament in Las Vegas on Tuesday, and the Volunteers took care of business. Maryland controlled the opening minutes, forcing Tennessee to play from beyond the three-point line. The Volunteers could get nothing going in the paint, and Maryland controlled everything early. The Terrapins held a 23-16 lead at the halfway mark of the first half. And then Dai Dai Ames got going. Ames was the spark-plug Tennessee needed, pouring in 15 first half points. Without him, Tennessee is likely looking at a double-digit deficit at halftime. With him, Tennessee took a 35-33 lead into the break. Tennessee continued their late first-half pace out of the break. Ames put Tennessee up 49-42 off of a great feed out of the paint from DeWayne Brown. The Vols’ defense set in, and suddenly Maryland had no answers. The Terps couldn’t hit anything from three-point range, and Tennessee wasn’t allowing any attempts from anywhere else. What felt like a sure Tennessee win was quickly in question after a rash of turnovers. Maryland clawed back thanks to some careless play from the Volunteers, with DJ Wagner putting the Terps back into contention. A 13-point lead was cut to four, and Tennessee suddenly needed an answer. A chaotic sequence resulted in Terrence Hill leaving the game with an injury. Troy Henderson would enter in his place. Hill would quickly return after a scare. Miles Rubin came up with a couple of massive defensive stops and a bucket to take Tennessee’s lead back to six points. Rubin’s assist to Brown would make it and eight-point game. Maryland had opportunities, but Tennessee had an answer at every turn. Tennessee held on to win, 72-64. Ames led the way with 24 points on 9-10 shooting. “I’m really proud of (Ames) because, you know what, he’s an everyday guy in practice,” Rick Barnes said after the game. “He’s trying to get better every day. And he’s learning me a little bit, obviously. And we know one thing, he’s a high-level competitor. We know he’s going to do what’s necessary and whatever we ask him to do.” Tennessee lost the rebounding and turnover battle, but they forced Maryland into 27 three-point attempts. The Terps made just three of those, dooming their offensive effort for the day. Tennessee moves on to face Iowa State on Thanksgiving day at 3:30 p.m. ET.

item.title: Chris Canty says the Indianapolis Colts are an ‘absolute embarrassment’ after Daniel Jones release
item.description: Photo by Justin Casterline/Getty Images The Indianapolis Colts made the surprising decision to cut Daniel Jones less than 24 hours after their loss to the Houston Texans last week. Jones had not been amazing this season, ranking 19th for passing yards and joint-27th for touchdowns. But the fact the Colts made the call under two weeks after the November trade deadline was pretty odd. Chris Canty has now commented on that decision, revealing that the Colts had the chance to trade the quarterback to the Baltimore Ravens and potentially the Minnesota Vikings. Chris Canty thinks the Colts don’t know ‘how to run a football franchise’ But after they snubbed both teams, Canty, speaking via ESPN, has come to the conclusion that Indianapolis don’t know how to run a football franchise and are an ‘absolute embarrassment’. He said: “The Colts have no idea how to run a football franchise. No clue. They released Daniel Jones. And this is after the Ravens offered a fourth-round pick and a conditional fifth-round pick for Daniel Jones, following their loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars on Thursday night in Week 9. “Now, I spoke to Adam Schefter this morning. He said that the Minnesota Vikings checked in with the Colts on Daniel Jones’ availability, and the Colts didn’t even give the Vikings a price for Daniel Jones. And for them to release him weeks later and get nothing for him, that is an absolute embarrassment.” This is not the first time the Colts’ non-playing personalities have been questioned in 2026. Carlie Irsay-Gordon has defended her ownership style amid perceived micromanagement of the coaching staff and her regular appearances on the sidelines during games. Now, the decision to get rid of Jones without receiving anything in return is likely to be used by detractors as another way to criticise the higher-ups. In this case, however, it is easy to see why people are not happy. The Colts are already 3-8 for the season and are now expected to spend the rest of the campaign with Anthony Richardson Sr. as their starting quarterback. Richardson is only 24 and during the one year he played more than 10 games in the NFL (2024), he had a worryingly low 47.7% completion rate in 11 appearances. Still, it will be interesting to see how he fares against the New York Giants on Sunday. item.title: Martha Firestone Ford, granddaughter of Harvey Firestone, dies at 101
item.description: Martha Firestone Ford, Akron native and former principal owner and current chair emeritus of the Detroit Lions , has died at 101. She was the granddaughter of Harvey S. Firestone, founder of Firestone Tire and Rubber Company in Akron. The Lions announced Ford's death in a story posted to their official website on Tuesday, Nov. 24 . The article indicated Ford had "passed away at her home surrounded by her loving family." "It is with heavy hearts that we acknowledge the passing of Martha Firestone Ford," the Lions wrote in a statement. "Mrs. Ford inspired us all as a pillar of the Detroit community and the passionate matriarch of the Detroit Lions football team." "She will always be remembered for her fierce loyalty to her family, her community and the city of Detroit," they added. "Her presence on our sideline, in our building, and in our community will be greatly missed. We wish the entire Ford and Firestone families peace in this time of mourning." Ford spent more than 60 years as the owner of the Lions. She and her husband, William Clay Ford, purchased the team in 1963. She took over sole control of the franchise after her husband's death in 2014, serving just over six years in that capacity before transitioning to her emeritus role in June 2020. Her husband was the grandson of Henry Ford, founder of Ford Motor Company and inventor of the Model T automobile. Ford is survived by her four children, all of whom hold roles within the Lions organization. That includes principal owner Sheila Ford Hamp, owner and vice chair Martha Ford Morse, owner and vice chair William Clay Ford Jr. and owner and vice chair Elizabeth Ford Kontulis. Martha Firestone Ford net worth According to Forbes , Ford's net worth was estimated to be $1.4 billion in 2019. Who is Sheila Ford Hamp? item.title: Skoda considers WRC Rally1 update kit for 2027
item.description: Motorsport photo Skoda Motorsport is considering developing a Rally1 kit, enabling its Rally2 car to contest the World Rally Championship top tier next year. New technical regulations for 2027 afford Rally2 manufacturers the opportunity to upgrade their machinery to Rally1 classification through the FIA’s update kit launched in June this year. The kit, costing €7,500, comprises new front bumpers and fenders and an upgraded rear wing. The car will be 10 kilograms lighter than the standard Rally2 car. It will also feature a 33mm turbo restrictor in line with the 2027 pure Rally1 machines that will offer a 10-15 horsepower advantage over a current Rally2 car. Under the FIA regulations, manufacturers that choose to develop new Rally1 machines have to enter at least 10 WRC rounds in 2027 with a minimum of two cars. Skoda has grown to become a dominant player in the Rally2 scene, and this year it guided Robert Virves to the WRC2 drivers’ crown. However, should Skoda commit to the kit, an upgraded car would not be ready for January's opening round of the season in Monte Carlo. "The kit is something we are considering but there is no final decision now. It is definitely not possible to manage that for Rallye Monte Carlo,” said a spokesperson from Skoda Motorsport. item.title: 'I'll be spending Christmas on a rowing boat in the Atlantic'
item.description: Liv Stocks will be attempting to set a world record [Liv Stocks] A rower in a team bidding to break a world record is preparing to spend her Christmas in the middle of the Atlantic Ocean. Liv Stocks, 23, is part of a trio attempting to row about 3,000 miles (about 4,800km) unassisted from the Canary Islands to Antigua. The team – which also includes Jenna Vincent and Meg Neely – will be competing in the 2026 World's Toughest Row as they try to be the youngest female crew to complete the challenge. "I've got a waxed cheese for Christmas Day," says Stocks, from Hive, near Howden, East Yorkshire. "So I'll be sitting on a boat, in the middle of the Atlantic, eating a round of cheese like an apple, which is going to be quite novel. "We've got some silly little hats and maybe a little drink of something each as well that we'll take with us... For most of the day, we'll just be rowing as normal, other than maybe the hour or two that we take off the oars to spend together." Jenna Vincent, Liv Stocks and Meg Neely will face sleep deprivation and "anything up to 30ft waves" [Liv Stocks] The women, who call themselves Just Row With It, will be raising money for charity. Stocks is supporting A Shining Light, a Howden-based charity set up to support the NHS, and Teenage Cancer Trust following the death of her schoolfriend Luke Stevens from bone cancer in 2021. The Atlantic challenge has been three years in the making and Stocks says she hopes her adventure will inspire other young people to take on their own challenges. "It's been a long road to get here, and in the past year it's been a real focus on water training, safety drills, safety courses. A lot of preparation goes into this," she says. "Breaks [will be] few and far between. The three hours on the oars will be three hours of straight rowing, maybe stopping occasionally for a quick drink or bites to eat, and then three hours off." Stocks says she hopes the night will include "a good sort of two and a half hours of sleep", but there will also be "cooking, cleaning, things like that" to do. "It really is going to be a true challenge of sleep, physical, mental – all of those different things wrapped into one," she predicts. The team are flying out to the Canary Islands on Saturday [Liv Stocks] The women are aiming to complete the race in about 45 days, but they're taking enough provisions for 60. "I think one of the reasons why I personally am doing this is because I feel like modern life is just so fast-paced," she says. "So I'm really looking forward to switching off and life becoming a very simple [one] of, literally, just eat, sleep, row, repeat. "I think it's really difficult in modern life – that feeling of facing fear head-on and really finding your limit." The trio will fly out to the Canary Islands on Saturday and will spend two weeks carrying out their final checks of the boat and getting prepped before starting their challenge on 12 December.
